description: Turn one food or drink photo into ads for listings and social feeds. Get watermark-free clips in minutes, not weeks, at far less cost than a kitchen shoot.
h1: Make AI Food and Drink Product Videos That Drive Cravings
lead: Hungry shoppers decide fast. Turn one food or drink photo into a clear package reveal, serving moment or product video that makes the next bite easy to imagine.
card: Serving scenes, package reveals and product videos from one food photo.
intro: Show the package clearly, then use a serving scene to show the product’s color, texture, or portion. A cold brew needs beads of condensation on the glass, a hot sauce needs a drizzle over tacos, and granola can be shown with a bowl of milk and berries. Packaging matters just as much, because that is what shoppers look for on a store shelf and in a delivery app.

Send in a clean package photo and describe one serving moment: a can cracking open over ice, a cookie snapping in half or honey dripping onto toast. Choose a 6-, 10-, 15-, or 30-second vertical clip for a social ad, or use a square photo for a listing.

faq.q: Will my ingredient list and nutrition facts look right in the image?
faq.a: Don't rely on the image for that. Small print on packaging may not come out exactly as printed, and ingredients, allergens, and nutrition facts should always match your real package. If buyers need to see them, use a clear photo of the actual label.

faq.q: Can I show a drink being poured if I only have a photo of the can?
faq.a: Yes. Describe the glass, the ice, and the color of the liquid, like "amber iced tea poured over ice in a tall glass." The more precise you are about color and texture, the closer the pour looks to your real drink.

faq.q: How long should a food video be for TikTok?
faq.a: 6 or 10 seconds covers a single moment like a pour or a first bite. Choose 15 seconds for two moments, such as the pack opening and the plated food, or 30 seconds for a longer serving story.

faq.q: Should I spray water on my can for a cold, fresh look?
faq.a: No need. Ask for condensation in your description instead, then wipe off fingerprints and photograph the dry can near a window with the light coming from the side.

faq.q: Can I run the clips as paid food and drink ads?
faq.a: Yes. Downloaded clips are watermark-free and licensed for commercial use, including paid ads and delivery-app listings. Keep nutrition, allergen, and ingredient claims to the real label, since small print in the clip may not be exact.

faq.q: Do I need a creator or a filming kitchen?
faq.a: No for these clips. The hands, adult creator, and setting are generated from your package photo at a per-clip credit cost. For a real customer tasting or an original concept, you can still film one separately.
